SEPARATE FROM LIVE CAPTURE

Test the current payload with a simulated capture, or open a saved matrix photograph. Live camera data and results stay separate.

Both variants use the same payload, reference grid, FEC, capture count, noise seeds, and interference trajectory. With five minimum samples and four extra captures, each phase gets nine observations: a seven-slot pool fills and then replaces its two oldest observations. The test continues after a successful decode to keep comparison budgets equal. Color fitting happens in each exposure before evidence is combined. Curvature changes the bands, not matrix geometry. Drift also varies the selected blur. These are synthetic stressors, not a physical screen/sensor model. A single uploaded photo uses its own current-frame references without phase fusion.

Local device

Field guide

Live link: Both keeps a large outgoing matrix and a small camera alignment window. The camera never covers matrix cells or markers. Display hides the receiver; Receive makes the camera large.

Image lab: loopback and uploaded matrix photographs use their own decoder, sequence state, and content viewer. Switching workspaces does not clear live results. Camera analysis pauses while the live workspace is hidden and resumes when you return.

Content: an eight-byte descriptor identifies raw bytes, UTF-8 text, PNG, JPEG, or PCM WAV. It lives inside the CRC-protected monochrome header of every frame. Data cells carry interleaved content, parity, and final padding. This bench supports one current format only, OBM5: reload both devices after updating; old saved matrices are not supported. Audio never autoplays.

Current-frame references: a one-cell rainbow grid separates data blocks of up to 4, 8, or 16 cells. These known cells estimate local colors in the same capture. Off uses only the outside palette strips. Reference cells consume capacity but do not increase the selected matrix size. Narrow-band interference can still vary between references and data.

Phases: each logical data frame has 1, 2, 4, 8, or 16 phases. Identical repetitions provide the control experiment. Palette permutations change physical colors through a public mapping; a full cycle of as many phases as palette colors visits every physical color once. Smaller palettes repeat mappings when phases exceed colors. Reference colors remain known and fixed. The monochrome header identifies each phase and its nominal hold time.

Continuous evidence: each capture is rectified and color-corrected independently, and its palette mapping is undone before evidence is combined. Robust mode selects the five most consistent observations per cell from a rolling seven-candidate pool by default. The pool keeps accepting new samples and expires old ones by age, so a wrong early consensus can be replaced. An ordinary mean decoder runs on the same evidence as a control. Mean and median modes are also available. RGB is never averaged across different palette mappings.

Progressive attempts: fusion starts after the configured number of sufficiently sampled phases (four by default, capped at the transmitted phase count), then retries as evidence changes. Available phases receive equal weight. The receiver skips 300 ms after a detected phase change. Phase retention accounts for the transmitted cycle timing. Large profiles may retain fewer samples or phases to stay within the evidence budget; the actual limits and readiness are displayed. Reset clears all evidence.

Error correction: shortened Reed–Solomon codewords carry 16 or 32 parity bytes. Ordinary RS corrects up to half as many erroneous bytes. Erasure-assisted decoding marks low-confidence bytes as unknown and tries bounded alternatives: 2e + s ≤ parity, where e is remaining erroneous bytes and s is erased bytes per codeword. Incorrect erasure choices consume capacity. Round-robin interleaving distributes adjacent bytes across codewords. Every accepted candidate must pass CRC; CRC detects corruption but cannot locate errors or authenticate a sender.

Device baseline: use Diagnostic, seed 1234, 64 × 64, 16 colors, one data frame, an 8-cell grid, RS 32, eight permuted phases, Robust with five minimum samples and two overhead, first attempt after four phases, erasure-assisted RS, 0.25 phases/s, and 1080p. Compare four, eight, and sixteen phases; compare Robust with Mean at the same acquisition time; then compare erasure-assisted with ordinary RS. Reset the receiver between newly generated sequences and settings changes when measuring time to recovery.

Measurements: the comparison separates one exposure, ordinary phase fusion, and robust phase fusion, with border and local color estimates for each. Raw errors include data and parity cells before correction, excluding references. Truth is used only after classification. Reports record CRC passes before correction, ordinary RS passes, extra erasure-assisted passes, first verified capture, and phase sampling limits. Repeated windows overlap and are correlated. First verified timing in the lab is processing time, not optical link speed. Each phase variant uses the same exposure budget even after success.

Resolution: choose up to 4K next to the camera selector. The requested size is a preference; the app reports the actual capture size and samples at that resolution. Higher resolution takes more processing time. Stop/restart or change resolution to clear temporal samples while preserving received content.

Images: PNG is useful for small graphics; JPEG often saves bytes for photos. Files are sent unchanged. Use small files or increase the frame limit, palette, or grid size.

Audio: WAV with mono/stereo 8- or 16-bit PCM needs no codec library, but is larger than compressed audio. Short mono clips are a practical starting point. A built-in sample is available in transmission settings.

Frames: Play cycles through up to eight data frames. Each data frame has its configured phase cycle; phases do not consume the eight-frame content limit. Receivers accept out-of-order frames and duplicates. Reset the corresponding receiver for a new sequence. There are no optical acknowledgments yet.

Capture: include all four markers and both palette strips. Start with 32 cells and 4 colors. Glare, clipping, blur, and low camera resolution can prevent decoding; aim for at least four camera pixels per cell.

Camera access: use HTTPS or localhost. A plain HTTP LAN URL usually cannot use a camera. Open the app as a full page if an embedded view blocks access.

Privacy and integrity: processing stays in this browser. CRC32 detects capture errors; it does not authenticate a sender. The separate Crypto Lab tests proof generation and verification. Optical proof exchange is a later integration step.
